effective_or_revised: Original Effective Date 02/15/01; Reviewed 07/23/26; Revised 08/15/26 (12 pages)
sections_in_order: Header block (policy number, Original Effective Date, Reviewed, Revised)
criteria_location: Position Statement pp.2-4: CMN note, a lettered A-G etiology list of end-stage liver disease, then separate one-line coverage statements (polycystic liver, hilar cholangiocarcinoma, hepatoblastoma, retransplant, combined liver-kidney), a does-not-meet list, an investigational list, and advisory contraindications.
procedures_covered: Liver transplant, cadaver or living donor (CPT 47135)

logic.top_level: pathways: lettered etiology categories A-G (any-of), HCC with ONE of three tumor-size schemes, plus separate standalone indications

k_of_n.quote: Primary hepatocellular carcinoma with ONE of the following: ... Milan criteria ... UCSF Expanded Criteria ... UNOS Stage T2 Criteria

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Three places: 'does not meet the definition of medical necessity for' (HCC beyond liver; candidate not approved by institution's transplant committee); an 'experimental or investigational' list (intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors metastatic to liver); and advisory 'Potential contraindications ... (subject to the judgment of the transplant center)'.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Retransplant has its own any-of list: 'Primary graft non-function; Hepatic artery thrombosis; Chronic rejection; Ischemic type biliary lesions ...; Recurrent non-neoplastic disease-causing late graft failure'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Etiologies of end-stage liver disease include, but are not limited to:
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Open-ended list ('not limited to'), so the A-G list cannot be treated as exhaustive; E 'Inborn errors of metabolism', F 'Trauma and toxic reactions', G 'Miscellaneous' are category names with no members.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: A single tumor 2 cm or greater, and up to 5 cm or less, OR 2 to 3 tumors 1 cm or greater, and up to 3 cm or less and without extrahepatic spread or macrovascular invasion
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Unclear whether 'without extrahepatic spread' applies to both alternatives or only the last.

requirement_kinds.quote: carefully selected individuals with end-stage liver failure resulting from irreversible liver damage
A single tumor 5 cm or less, OR 2 to 3 tumors that are 3 cm or less (Milan criteria)
The transplant candidate is not approved by the transplant committee for the institution
Submit a completed Certificate of Medical Necessity (CMN)
Combined liver-kidney transplantation ... in those who qualify for liver transplantation and have advanced irreversible kidney disease

thresholds.quote: A single tumor 5 cm or less
A single tumor 6.5 cm or less, OR up to 3 tumors 4.5 cm or less, and a total tumor size of 8 cm or less

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: CPT codes for recipient, donor and backbench work listed with descriptors; none mapped to indications.

vague_terms.problem: asterisk footnote not clearly resolved in extracted text.

extraction_hazards: Bullets are either the private-use character U+F0B7 or U+2022 depending on the document (the fusion guideline uses both), never '-' or '*'; nested bullets use other glyphs ('o') or only deeper indentation
Hyperlink navigation bar after the disclaimer is flattened into a 2-3 row text block that looks like headings
Form-feed (\f) page breaks can fall mid-list or immediately before a section heading, so '^HEADING' regexes can miss; no running headers/footers or page numbers to strip
Lettered list A-G mixes category headings with bullets, so category vs member depth depends on glyph/indent
Two-line 'OR' alternatives inside one bullet in the HCC list
Compound heading 'Liver Transplant and Combined Liver-Kidney Transplant' wraps to two Subject lines
No DEFINITIONS-colon problem but definitions are alphabetical glossary of anatomy, not criteria
interesting_structures: Three alternative tumor staging systems (Milan, UCSF, UNOS T2) as alternate leaves
Same advisory contraindication list as heart and pancreas docs (family template with organ-specific edits)
Three-way outcome vocabulary: meets / does not meet / experimental

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: Etiology list and HCC any-of are clean; open-ended 'not limited to' list, empty category names, and advisory contraindications need human judgment.
